Since Bun 1.5, top-level `vi.mock()` and `jest.mock()` calls are [hoisted](/test/mocks#hoisting--preloading) above the file's imports. An import that loads the module calls the factory before the file's variables are initialized, which throws a `ReferenceError`, or reads `undefined` from a `var`.

The rule reports a variable in a factory if the file imports the mocked module, or another file of the project, before the variable is initialized. It also reports an import that the factory reads, if the mocked module is imported first.

`--fix` wraps the value in `vi.hoisted()`, along with the variables it reads, and imports `vi` if it has to. It changes nothing if the value needs an import, a function from the file or an `await`, or if code above the mock can change it, as with `process.env`. For `jest.mock()` in a file that doesn't import from `bun:test` it's a suggestion, because Jest has no `vi`.

`bun lint --upgrade` runs this rule. See [Upgrade Bun](/lint#upgrade-bun).

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. To turn it on:

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/no-unhoisted-mock-variables" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad */}
```ts
import { vi } from "vitest";
import { checkout } from "./checkout";

const charge = vi.fn();
vi.mock("./payments", () => ({ charge }));

checkout();
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { vi } from "vitest";
import { checkout } from "./checkout";

const charge = vi.hoisted(() => vi.fn());
vi.mock("./payments", () => ({ charge }));

checkout();
```

A primitive literal is hoisted with the mock, and a function in the factory reads the variable later:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { vi } from "vitest";
import { checkout } from "./checkout";

const currency = "EUR";
const charge = vi.fn();
vi.mock("./payments", () => ({ currency, charge: (amount: number) => charge(amount) }));

checkout();
```
